newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Calm returns to PNG stocks.
newsitem.headline: Calm returns to PNG stocks.

text.p: Calm returned to Papua New Guinea's (PNG) Australian-listed stocks on Tuesday after a sharp sell-off 24 hours earlier when investors got the jitters over an army attempt to force the prime minister from office.
Order was restored on Tuesday, when the PNG army chief who turned against Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan over a plan to use foreign mercenaries on Bougainville island agreed to step down.

PNG government-controlled resource group Orogen Minerals Ltd, which fell about seven percent on Monday, ended steady at A$3.20 (US$2.53) on Tuesday, while oil producer Oil Search Ltd ended 10 cents up at A$2.70, after Monday's 8.5 percent fall.
"It is a bit of a storm in a tea-cup," said Ben Semos, an institutional dealer with Wilson HTM.
"I think our market has completely over-reacted to what happened up there," said Semos, who has PNG institutional clients. "Although the market will be on tenterhooks over the next 48 hours."

Other PNG stocks also clawed back lost ground, including Niugini Mining Ltd, which ended four cents up at A$3.00 after losing nine cents on Monday, and Lihir Gold Ltd, which closed two cents firmer at A$2.12 after a seven-percent fall.
Investors had oversold stocks that had nothing to do with the central issue in the South Pacfic nation -- the conflict on Bougainville island, Semos said.

Shares in Bougainville Copper Ltd, which is controlled by the world's largest miner RTZ-CRA group and owns the disputed Panguna copper mine on Bougainville, were one cent up at 56 cents after Monday's 8.33-percent slide.
The Panguna copper mine was shut down in 1989 at the start of the rebellion when local landowners were refused a greater interest in the mine.
Investors were waiting for an end to the current PNG crisis before they take their next cue, brokers said.
"There is no longer widespread panic out there as people are waiting for some sort of resolution," one Sydney broker said.
